objectives.text: Keep the transition inside the state that the 2021 coup began. A constitution approved by referendum in September 2025 dropped the limits on junta members standing; Gen. Mamadi Doumbouya won the 28 December 2025 presidential election with 86.7% of the vote (preliminary 86.72%), a seven-year mandate upheld by the Supreme Court on 4 January 2026. The main opposition was largely excluded; Alpha Conde and Cellou Dalein Diallo are in exile.

grand_strategy.reading: Guinea's grand strategy is to turn the 2021 coup into a constitutional mandate and to live off bauxite and, from December 2025, Simandou iron ore, with China as the main owner of the new mine and a major buyer of the old export. Its weak point is the region: ECOWAS suspended it after the coup, and no source found for this card shows the suspension lifted. Not verified for this card: Mali and the AES, Russia and Rusal, the US aid cut, the Simandou railway and port, and the links to Sierra Leone and Senegal beyond the 1990s refugee and ECOMOG record.

stances.note: ECOWAS suspended Guinea after the coup of 5 September 2021 (BBC, 9 September 2021). Guinea stays in the bloc and cooperates on the file out of necessity, with visible friction: reluctant_partner is our reading of that structure (C); no source uses the word. Bond none: pure interest, nothing sourced underneath. Gap: whether the suspension was lifted after the 28 December 2025 election is not verified in this pass.

stances.note: Diplomatic relations date from 13 February 1959 (State Department relations page, 2018). Guinea signed a bilateral immunity agreement with the US under Article 98 of the Rome Statute (per Wikipedia's citation, not opened here); transactional, no alignment: partner is our reading (C). The US condemned the 2021 coup (State Department, 5 September 2021), so the relation is not warm. Trend stable only because no source in this pass records a change; the US aid cut is not verified and no cooling is recorded. Bond none is our reading. Gap: the aid cut and the current US-Guinea agreements need primary sources.
